pages.text: By noon, the zinc roof is too hot to touch and the shadows have almost disappeared. The cause is 150 million kilometres away. The Sun is a star. It looks different from the other stars only because it is so close. It is a huge ball of hot, glowing gas, mostly hydrogen and helium. About 1.3 million Earths would fit inside it, and it holds 99.8 per cent of all the mass in the Solar System. Its surface is about 5,500 °C. Its centre is far hotter, about 15 million °C. There, hydrogen nuclei are squeezed together to make helium. This process is called nuclear fusion. It releases the energy that reaches us as light and heat. Never look straight at the Sun. It can damage your eyes in seconds.

pages.text: Astronomers classify stars by temperature, colour, and brightness. The hottest stars shine blue-white. Cooler stars shine orange or red. The Sun is in between. Its class is written G2V, and stars of this kind are often called yellow dwarfs. The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old, roughly halfway through its life. Is it a big star? That depends on what you compare it with. Most stars in our galaxy are red dwarfs, which are smaller and dimmer than the Sun. But giant stars exist too. The red supergiant Betelgeuse is hundreds of times wider than the Sun.

pages.text: Gravity is a force that pulls objects towards each other. The more mass an object has, the stronger its pull. Because the Sun is so massive, its gravity controls everything around it. Each planet is moving sideways at great speed. Earth travels about 30 kilometres every second. Without the Sun’s gravity, a planet would fly off in a straight line. With it, the planet’s path bends into a curve around the Sun. That curved path is called an orbit. To revolve is to travel once around an orbit. Earth takes one year to revolve around the Sun.

pages.text: Eight planets orbit the Sun. The four nearest are small and rocky: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars. Beyond Mars lies the asteroid belt, a ring of rocky bodies. Then come two gas giants, Jupiter and Saturn, and two ice giants, Uranus and Neptune. To remember the order, try this sentence: My Very Energetic Mother Just Sold Us Nkatie. Most planets have moons. A moon is a natural satellite: an object that orbits a planet. Earth has one. Saturn has the most. In 2025, astronomers confirmed 128 more, bringing its total to 274.

A moon is a natural satellite: an object that orbits a planet.
Earth has one.
Saturn has the most.
In 2025, astronomers confirmed 128 more, bringing its total to 274.
pages.alt: The eight planets in order from the Sun, each labelled: four small rocky planets, the asteroid belt, two gas giants, and two ice giants.

pages.text: Pluto was discovered in 1930 and was called the ninth planet for 76 years. Then astronomers began finding other icy worlds beyond Neptune. One of them, Eris, has even more mass than Pluto. Was Eris a tenth planet? In 2006, the International Astronomical Union agreed on a definition. A planet must orbit the Sun. It must be massive enough for its own gravity to pull it into a round shape. And it must have cleared other objects out of its orbit. Pluto passes the first two tests but fails the third. It was reclassified as a dwarf planet.

pages.text: We are still learning about our star. In 2018, NASA launched the Parker Solar Probe to study the Sun from close up. On 24 December 2024, it flew through the Sun’s outer atmosphere, only about 6 million kilometres above the surface. No spacecraft has ever been closer. At that moment it was moving at about 690,000 kilometres an hour, faster than any other object people have built. Its measurements help scientists understand the solar wind, a stream of charged particles that the Sun blows out in all directions. The solar wind matters on Earth. Strong bursts can disturb satellites, radio signals, and power lines.

activities.question: Where does the Sun’s energy come from?
options: Coal and gas burning inside it
Nuclear fusion, in which hydrogen nuclei join to make helium

activities.question: Why does Earth not fly off into space in a straight line?
options: The Sun’s gravity bends Earth’s path into an orbit
The Moon pushes Earth towards the Sun

activities.question: Why is Pluto classified as a dwarf planet?
options: It does not orbit the Sun
It has not cleared other objects out of its orbit

glossary.definition: Nuclear fusion: light nuclei, such as hydrogen, join to form heavier ones and release energy.
A force that pulls objects towards each other; more mass means a stronger pull.
The curved path of one object around another.
An object that orbits a planet; a moon is a natural satellite.
